activity.notes: Menander I was the most prominent Indo-Greek king in the Indian territories. Encyclopaedia Iranica uses 165-130 BCE but emphasizes that Indo-Greek succession chronology rests heavily on numismatic reconstruction; ATLAS therefore keeps both boundaries approximate.

sources.title: INDO-GREEK DYNASTY
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica identifies Menander I as the most important Greek king in Indian territories and dates him 165-130 BCE, while noting the numismatic basis of Indo-Greek chronology.
